title: Northwind Logistics - Discovery Call
segments: Jenna
Thanks for making time today, Greg and Linda. I'm Jenna, I lead the account team here, and Aisha from our product group is joining to answer the technical questions.
Greg
Happy to be here. Just so you know, we're in the middle of our budget cycle, so this is a good time to be talking.
Jenna
That's great to hear. Before I show anything, I'd love to understand what's going on at Northwind. What made you take this call?
Greg

Honestly, visibility. We move about forty thousand shipments a month across nine carriers, and my ops team lives in spreadsheets. When a customer calls asking where their freight is, it takes twenty minutes to find out.
Linda
And it's not only the time. The data is stale by the time it reaches the spreadsheet. We pull carrier updates in by hand twice a day.
Jenna
Twice a day. So if a truck is delayed at ten, the customer might not hear until the afternoon.
Greg
Exactly. We lost an account in June because of that. They found out about a delay from their own customer before we told them.
Jenna
I'm sorry to hear that. How many people on your team are doing that manual tracking today?
Greg
Six full time, and probably another four who do it part time when things get busy.
Aisha
Linda, can I ask how those carrier updates arrive? Is it email, EDI, portals?
Linda
A bit of everything. Four carriers have APIs, three send EDI files, and two we only get through a web portal that someone logs into.
Aisha
That's a pretty typical mix. We support all three, and for portal-only carriers we have a connector that handles the login and polling so nobody has to do it by hand.
Linda
That would be a big deal. What about security? Our carriers' portal credentials are sensitive.
Aisha
Credentials are encrypted at rest and never shown in the UI once they're saved. We're also SOC 2 Type II certified, and I can send the report after the call.
Linda
Please do. Our security team will want to review that before we go any further.
Jenna
Absolutely, I'll make sure that goes out today. Greg, let me show you what the tracking view looks like.
Jenna
This is a live shipment. You can see every carrier event on a single timeline, and the estimated arrival updates automatically when something changes.
Greg
Okay, that's much cleaner than what we have. Can my customers see this as well, or only my team?
Aisha
Both. You can share a branded tracking page per shipment or per customer account, and they can subscribe to alerts by email or text.
Greg
That alone might have saved the June account. What does the alerting look like if something goes wrong?
Aisha
You define rules. For example, notify the account owner if a shipment is more than two hours behind its estimate, or if it sits at a facility longer than twelve hours.
Greg
I like that. Linda, you'd be the one integrating this. How would you feel about it?
Linda
Depends on the effort. We're a small IT team. If it's a six month project, that's a no.
Aisha
Most customers with your carrier mix are live in about six weeks. The first two weeks are connecting carriers, then we run in parallel with your spreadsheets before you cut over.
Linda
Six weeks is manageable. Would we need to change our TMS?
Aisha
No. We sync with it through an API, so you keep your existing system and we sit alongside it. I can walk Linda through the integration docs separately.
Greg
Let's talk numbers then. Jenna, what's the ballpark?
Jenna

Pricing is based on monthly shipment volume. At forty thousand shipments you'd be in our growth tier. I'll put together a formal proposal, but I'd expect it to land between eight and ten thousand a month, all in.
Greg
That's within what I could get approved, especially if we can show the spreadsheet labor goes away. Six people at that cost is a lot more than ten thousand.
Jenna
I'd love to help you build that case. If you can share your current loaded cost for the tracking team, I'll model the savings with you.
Greg
I can get that from finance by Friday.
Linda
One more question. What happens if a carrier changes their portal? That seems fragile.
Aisha
It happens, and it's our job, not yours. We monitor the connectors continuously, and when one breaks our team fixes it, usually within a business day. You get a status notice while it's down.
Linda
That's reassuring. I've been burned by that with a previous vendor.
Jenna
Understood. Let's talk about next steps. I'd suggest three things. First, I send the SOC 2 report and the integration docs today.
Jenna
Second, Greg sends the loaded cost figures by Friday so I can build the savings model. Third, we schedule a technical session with Linda and Aisha next week.
Greg
That works. Can we also get a sandbox so Linda's team can try a couple of carriers?
Aisha
Yes, I'll set up a sandbox with your four API carriers so you can see real data flowing in. You'll have it by Monday.
Linda
Great. Tuesday afternoon would work for the technical session.
Jenna
I'll send an invite for Tuesday at two. Greg, any other concerns I should know about before we wrap up?
Greg
Only timing. If we're going to switch, I'd like to be live before peak season starts in November.
Jenna
Working backward from November, we'd need to sign by mid October. That's tight but doable if the security review goes quickly.
Greg
Let's aim for that. Thanks, this was more useful than I expected.
Jenna
Thank you both. I'll follow up with everything we discussed within the hour.
overview: Discovery call with Northwind Logistics, which ships roughly 40,000 shipments a month across nine carriers and tracks them by hand in spreadsheets. Stale data cost them an account in June. Aisha covered carrier integrations (API, EDI, and portal connectors), security (SOC 2 Type II, encrypted credentials), customer-facing tracking pages, and rule-based alerts. Linda's concern was integration effort; typical go-live is about six weeks alongside their existing TMS. Pricing is expected between $8k and $10k per month in the growth tier. Northwind wants to be live before November peak season, which means signing by mid October.
